# Lacuna v0.3.0

Lacuna `v0.3.0` completes the trading-realism milestone. It turns normalized trades and declared
market assumptions into inspectable evidence about commission, spread, slippage, impact, borrow,
cost sensitivity, break-even friction, liquidity participation, and nonlinear capacity erosion.

## Highlights

- Immutable, composable cost estimates with per-trade components, explicit units, assumptions,
  findings, fingerprints, and unknown-row preservation.
- Commission, observed/assumed spread, proportional/fixed/volatility slippage, participation and
  square-root impact, and annualized borrow models.
- Deterministic Cartesian stress grids or named correlated scenarios with component reconciliation,
  gross/net performance, turnover, sample support, and optional Sharpe.
- Monotonicity-checked bracketed break-even solving for P&L, return, Sharpe, and CAGR with a complete
  trace and no silent extrapolation.
- Point-in-time or explicitly retrospective liquidity diagnostics that keep missing, invalid, and
  future volume visible.
- Multi-scenario capacity curves over capital with participation constraints and unknown liquidity,
  never one false-precision capacity number.
- Hand-computed and planted fixtures, property invariants, Polars/pandas/Arrow equivalence, a
  versioned stress benchmark, and clean-wheel exercise of the new public path.
- A frozen additive `0.3.x` public contract that preserves supported `0.1.x` and `0.2.x` calls.

## Compatibility and distribution

This release keeps `AnalysisResult.schema_version == "1"` and adds `lacuna.costs` without removing
the earlier supported surfaces. It is distributed as checksummed GitHub Release artifacts because
the `lacuna` name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project. The release workflow builds and
smoke-tests CPython 3.11 stable-ABI wheels for Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS arm64, and Windows x86_64,
plus a source distribution and provenance attestations.

The full implementation record is in the
[changelog](https://github.com/eyenoticeall/Lacuna/blob/v0.3.0/CHANGELOG.md), and exact formulas,
temporal rules, failure modes, and interpretation limits are in the trading-costs methodology page.
